range.connector.why: No ICU/CLDR resource walked gives en a spoken range connector. CLDR writes only the separator: root NumberElements/latn/miscPatterns/range '{0}–{1}' and calendar/gregorian/intervalFormats/fallback '{0} – {1}' (ICU 78.3). Resources searched with no spoken connector: RBNF spellout/ordinal/duration, ICUDATA-unit, ICUDATA-lang, en NumberElements, fields, listPattern (dualplan-ranges 03, (N)); and calendar/gregorian in root, en and en_US, walked by tests/test_lexical_forms.py::test_calendar_walk_finds_no_en_range_connector: its intervalFormats patterns hold no literal word, and the words the subtree does hold join other things, not a range's two ends ('at' in DateTimePatterns%atTime and %relative, "{1} 'at' {0}"; 'week' and 'of' in availableFormats MMMMW and yw, "'week' W 'of' MMMM"). Which pattern is said is for the corpus to measure, not for this table

range.separator.why: hyphen-minus, ':' and 'x' between numbers are forms ICU writes nowhere in en (kal, 2026-09-28); en dash ranges come from icukit. Measured narrowly for ':': en's calendar/gregorian writes it between numbers only in time patterns, joining a clock's hour, minute and second (DateTimePatterns 'h:mm:ss', and the Hm and hm availableFormats and intervalFormats); the corpus reads a ':' between numbers that is not a valid clock 'to' (training shard 0: 1,419 'to', 41 silent; dualplan-ranges 03)

zero.words.why: the words a zero digit is said as, so readings that differ only there share their weight: RBNF's cardinal says 'zero' and its year rule 'oh'; the corpus says 'o' (kal, 2026-09-26)

zero.digit.why: the corpus says a zero digit 'o' (a date's zero is 'o' 47,752 times, 'oh' never); ICU has no digit rule that says 'o'

zero.minute.why: a zero-led minute ('10:05') is said 'oh five' or 'o five'; ICU's cardinal says 'five' and no ICU time pattern says the zero

zero.year.why: ICU's year rule says a zero-led second half 'oh' ('nineteen oh-eight'); the corpus says 'o' ('nineteen o eight')

clock.oclock.why: no CLDR form for an on-the-hour time said with o'clock

clock.hundred.why: the corpus reads a written on-the-hour 24-hour time ('20:00') 'twenty hundred'; no CLDR time pattern says 'hundred'

possessive.suffix.why: no CLDR possessive for a spelled run

separator.words.why: no CLDR spoken name for '@' in an address (ICU's character name is COMMERCIAL AT), and the corpus holds no email address to measure one

letter.vowels.why: a consonant-vowel key for acronym ranking, not a CLDR set

currency.units.why: CLDR's en CurrencyPlurals name each major unit with its region ('US dollar'/'US dollars', 'British pound', 'Japanese yen'), except EUR's 'euro'/'euros'; the table holds the corpus's bare major names for the other nine currencies, and every minor-unit name, which CLDR's currency data does not give. EUR's major row equals CLDR's and is here only because a row pairs the major name with the minor ('cent'); reading it from CLDR is filed. Each row is singular and plural, major then minor

currency.region_names.why: CLDR's en_US display name is 'US Dollar', not the corpus's region-expanded name; singular and plural

fraction.denominators.why: English RBNF names regular ordinals ('second', 'fourth') but carries neither of the corpus's fraction words; singular and plural by denominator

fraction.one.why: the corpus reads a whole and a single half or quarter with an article ('1 1/2' 'one and a half'); no CLDR pattern puts one there

ordinal.article.why: the corpus reads a Roman numeral or Roman ordinal with 'the' ('Henry II' 'the second', 'V.' 'the fifth'); no CLDR pattern puts an article before an ordinal

date.day_first.why: the corpus reads a day-first date as 'the eighteenth of September'; no CLDR date pattern supplies this spoken frame

sign.plus.why: a written plus is usually said and sometimes dropped; ICU spells no plus sign

numeral.plural.why: the English plural of a number word ('nineties', 'sixes', 'hundreds'); CLDR has no plural of a numeral. The first rule whose ending matches applies: drop 'strip' characters and add 'add', unless the character before the ending is in 'not_after'

duration.milliseconds.why: the corpus's race-time reading ('1:47.22' '... seconds and twenty two milliseconds'): 'and' before the milliseconds only, after ICU's unit list joins the rest

measure.per_plural.why: the corpus also puts the unit's plural after 'per' ('per square kilometers'); both unit forms are ICU's, and where the plural goes is the corpus's choice
